arXiv:2608.13906v1 [cs.IT] 14 Aug 2026

New lower bounds for constant-weight codes via seeded bit-swap tabu search

William Echols
Abstract

A binary constant-weight code is a set of binary words of length nn such that each word has exactly weight ww and is at least Hamming distance dd from every other word in the set. A⁡(n,d,w)A(n,d,w) denotes the maximum size of a binary constant-weight code with parameters (n,d,w)(n,d,w). Using seeded initialization with bit-swap tabu search, we found 124 new constructions that improve existing lower bounds for A⁡(n,d,w)A(n,d,w). As a corollary of stronger bounds on A⁡(n,8,8)A(n,8,8) for n∈{32,33,34,37}n\in\{32,33,34,37\}, we also improve lower bounds on kissing numbers τ32\tau_{32}, τ33\tau_{33}, τ34\tau_{34}, and τ37\tau_{37}.

1 Introduction

A binary constant-weight code is a set of binary words, where each word has length nn, Hamming weight ww, and is at least Hamming distance dd from every other word in the set. The Hamming distance of two binary words of length nn, denoted xx and yy, is defined to be dH​(x,y)=∑i=1n(xi⊕yi)d_{H}(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}\oplus y_{i}), and the Hamming weight of a given binary word xx is defined as wH​(x)=∑i=1nxiw_{H}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}. The maximum number of binary codewords of length nn and Hamming weight ww such that any two codewords are at least Hamming distance dd apart is denoted as A⁡(n,d,w)A(n,d,w).

Significant computational efforts have been used to construct codes for various choices of (n,d,w)(n,d,w), demonstrating lower bounds on A⁡(n,d,w)A(n,d,w) [2, 7, 9, 10]. In addition, existing codes for parameter set (n,d,w)(n,d,w) can be lengthened to find codes for (n+1,d,w)(n+1,d,w) or shortened to find codes for (n−1,d,w)(n-1,d,w) [2, 4]. We focus on initialization via seeding, from both equivalent and neighboring parameters, to find stronger lower bounds for A⁡(n,d,w)A(n,d,w).

Previous implementations of tabu search for the construction of constant-weight codes resulted in weaker bounds than known results and alternative metaheuristic algorithms [1, 7]. However, the formulation of a bit-swap tabu search by Rosin found new lower bounds for six constant-weight codes [8].

2 Methods

We modify Rosin’s approach [8] by warm-starting bit-swap tabu search; rather than initializing the search with ss randomly generated nn-bit words of weight ww, we instead seed the search using codewords from an existing code for the same or neighboring parameter set.

In the direct case, where the target has parameters (n,d,w)(n,d,w) and seeding uses an existing code SS of the same parameters and word count mm, we first construct a library composed of the existing codewords appended with an additional word vv chosen to minimize the aggregate distance-deficit penalty; we use a library rather than a single candidate code as there are multiple words with equivalent minimal-deficit penalties. Then, Rosin’s refined bit-swap tabu search is executed up to 4​|E|4|E| times with random samples from the library, where EE is the set of minimal-deficit words. We use Rosin’s tabu parameters unchanged [8] but omit the restart mechanism which would otherwise override the provided seed. Let W⁡(n,w)={x∈{0,1}n:∑i=1nxi=w}W(n,w)=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}:\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}=w\} be the set of binary words of length nn and Hamming weight ww. Direct seeded initialization is described in Algorithm 1.

We broaden the seeding concept to allow the strengthening of certificates with adjacent values of nn, as described in Algorithm 2. Neighbor-seeded initialization includes code lengthening, which uses an existing certificate for A⁡(n−1,d,w)A(n-1,d,w) to form words of length nn; these words then constitute the initial code for the bit-swap tabu search. Symmetrically, a certificate for A⁡(n+1,d,w)A(n+1,d,w) can be shortened on a zero-slice to seed a search for parameter set (n,d,w)(n,d,w). The intermediate code obtained by lengthening or shortening is usually smaller than the target size ss; we pad it to size ss by appending randomly chosen words of minimum penalty, at the cost of violating the minimum-distance property. Recomputing the minimal-deficit set EE after each insertion is computationally intensive; as a result, our implementation computes EE initially and samples from it uniformly with replacement. The bit-swap tabu search then repairs the padded set into a valid code. Both the lengthening and shortening techniques are well-known in the literature [2, 4] and have been used to construct lower bounds [3].

Since each successful run produces a new valid code, the algorithm can be applied successively to its own output. Varying the seeding method between iterations can additionally allow the search to escape local obstacles through the use of words from neighboring parameter sets.

3 Results

Table 1 lists 124 new constructions which were discovered with these methods. Each code improves a lower bound in Brouwer’s online table [3] and was verified with a separate program in the repository.

3.1 Constant-weight codes

As an immediate corollary of the codes in Table 1, appending a zero coordinate to our (28,8,6)(28,8,6) code gives A⁡(29,8,6)≥132A(29,8,6)\geq 132, and shortening our (48,8,6)(48,8,6) code on a zero-slice gives A⁡(47,8,6)≥588A(47,8,6)\geq 588. Each of these improves the previously listed bounds of 130 and 583, respectively [3].

3.2 Kissing numbers

A⁡(n,d)A(n,d) denotes the maximum size of a binary code such that all words have length nn and any two words are at least Hamming distance dd apart. In particular, the [32,17,8][32,17,8] binary linear code of Cheng and Sloane gives A⁡(32,8)≥217A(32,8)\geq 2^{17} [5].

From Edel et al. [6], we have the following lower bound on the kissing number τn\tau_{n}, where the chosen values of n0,n1,…,nμ∈ℕn_{0},n_{1},\ldots,n_{\mu}\in\mathbb{N} satisfy n≥n0n\geq n_{0} and ∀i∈{0,1,…,μ−1},ni≥4​ni+1≥1\forall i\in\{0,1,\ldots,\mu-1\},n_{i}\geq 4n_{i+1}\geq 1.

τn\displaystyle\tau_{n} ≥∑ν=0μA⁡(n,nν,nν)​A​(nν,⌈nν4⌉)\displaystyle\geq\sum_{\nu=0}^{\mu}A(n,n_{\nu},n_{\nu})A\left(n_{\nu},\left\lceil\frac{n_{\nu}}{4}\right\rceil\right) (1)

With choices (n,n0,n1,n2)=(32,32,8,2)(n,n_{0},n_{1},n_{2})=(32,32,8,2) and the previously-known lower bound A⁡(32,8,8)≥1659A(32,8,8)\geq 1659, we find

τ32\displaystyle\tau_{32} ≥A⁡(32,32,32)​A​(32,8)+A⁡(32,8,8)​A​(8,2)+A⁡(32,2,2)​A​(2,1)\displaystyle\geq A(32,32,32)A(32,8)+A(32,8,8)A(8,2)+A(32,2,2)A(2,1)
≥1⋅217+1659⋅27+496⋅22\displaystyle\geq 1\cdot 2^{17}+1659\cdot 2^{7}+496\cdot 2^{2}
≥345408\displaystyle\geq 345408

With the improvement of A⁡(32,8,8)≥1667A(32,8,8)\geq 1667, we can immediately strengthen the bound to τ32≥346432\tau_{32}\geq 346432. For n≥32n\geq 32, we can modify Equation (1) with choices (n0,n1,n2)=(32,8,2)(n_{0},n_{1},n_{2})=(32,8,2) to show

τn≥217+A⁡(n,8,8)⋅27+2​n​(n−1)\displaystyle\tau_{n}\geq 2^{17}+A(n,8,8)\cdot 2^{7}+2n(n-1) (2)

The new lower bounds along with their associated choices for n0,n1​…,nμn_{0},n_{1}\ldots,n_{\mu} are presented in Table 2.

Data Availability

The binary constant-weight codes referenced in Table 1 are publicly available at https://github.com/williamechols/cwc-seeded-tabu-search.
